---
title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Mental Health (Depression)"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Urban greenspace is valued as the depression cases it prevents. Paving over a city's nature
would raise its residents' depression risk; the cases that rise represents are the cases
today's greenness prevents, priced at the societal cost of one case. The base year is 2019.

⚠ Coverage is the 32 countries with a societal-cost estimate (Christensen et al. 2020), by
construction. Those costs arrive in international (PPP) dollars of mostly 2018 and are converted
to market 2019 USD by the shared price-level and CPI series, with the owner's PPP reading kept
beside the result. The counterfactual converts all urban nature to built land, following the
InVEST urban mental health model.

## Quantity

Per urban pixel on WorldPop's 1 km grid: observed depression cases (WHO prevalence times
population) times the prevented-cases factor $e^{-10 \ln(\text{RR}) \, \text{NDVI}} - 1$, the
InVEST model's dose-response at the pixel's annual NDVI, summed per country over the urban
settlement mask. The risk ratio comes from the Liu et al. 2023 meta-analytic odds ratio
(`health_depression_odds_ratio`, 0.931) converted by Zhang and Yu 1998 at the authors'
reference-group risk p0 = 0.115 (`health_depression_prevalence_nonexposed`), one value for every
country: RR = 0.931 / (1 − 0.115 + 0.115 × 0.931) = 0.938447 per 0.1 NDVI. p0 is the
health-record depression share in the lowest residential-NDVI quartile of Hystad et al. 2019, as
the write-up's equation 5 and the authors' run file both set it. The country's prevalence enters
only the case count.

⚠ Two points of the authors' method are not yet settled, and this note follows neither choice
silently:

- **Baseline prevalence for the case count.** The write-up specifies each country's GBD
  2023-release prevalence of depressive disorders for estimate year 2019 (all ages, both sexes,
  crude). The authors' script uses 5% in every country. That GBD table is not staged here, so the
  WHO 2015 country prevalence stays in place until the authors share the exact table.
- **The dose-response sign.** The authors' code computes PF = 1 − RR^(10 ΔNE), with ΔNE the 2019
  NDVI minus the no-vegetation NDVI. The write-up's prose defines ΔNE the same way, but its
  equation 4 defines it as scenario minus baseline. Its equation 2, PF = 1/RR − 1, then gives a
  different number under each definition. This note keeps $e^{-10 \ln(\text{RR}) \, \text{NDVI}} - 1$
  until the authors confirm the intended equation.

## Price

The societal cost of one depression case -- healthcare plus productivity losses -- from the
owner's staged Christensen et al. 2020 extract. The extract reports international (PPP) dollars,
so each country's cost is multiplied by its price-level ratio (market GDP over PPP GDP, the
account's shared series) and then by the US CPI factor from the cost year to 2019, giving market
2019 USD.

## Valuation

$$
\text{GEP}_i = c_i \; x_i \sum_{j \in \text{urban}} n_j \left(e^{-10 \ln(\text{RR})\,\text{NDVI}_j} - 1\right)
$$

with $c_i$ the cost per case, $x_i$ the prevalence, $n_j$ the pixel population and RR the one
risk ratio at p0. The urban sums carry RR inside the exponential, so a sum built at another
conversion cannot be rescaled; the run refuses a saved sum whose signature does not match. The
author's high-resolution results file is carried beside the result as the comparison point;
its spatial scope is an open question, so the run log reports the gap rather than anchoring.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in constant 2019 USD. Of the 250, 32 carry a value, 0 are computed zeros, and 218 rows are missing, kept as missing rather than zero because an input carries no data for those countries. A zero means the computation returned zero. A missing row means the data to compute one is absent.

## Inputs

All paths and parameters come from `es_parameters.csv` under the `health_depression` service
key. The three rasters (population, NDVI, urban mask) are the hypertension strand's staged
files, shared deliberately; the disease tables (prevalence, costs, odds ratio, the author's
reference) are this service's own, each with a source row beside it.
